prompt: A BD rep explained a proposed stack to a non-technical client. Mark the statements that are wrong or misleading.

task.prompt: A BD rep explained a proposed stack to a non-technical client. Mark the statements that are wrong or misleading.

segments.text: We will build the mobile app in Flutter, so one codebase covers iPhone and Android.
The backend runs on Node.js and stores data in PostgreSQL.
PostgreSQL is a design tool for making screens.
segments.issue: PostgreSQL is a database, not a design tool.

segments.text: We will host it on a cloud provider like AWS, so it can scale as users grow.
Because we use React, the app will never have bugs.
segments.issue: No framework prevents bugs; quality comes from testing and process.

segments.text: The admin dashboard is a web app built in React.

prompt: Rank these ways to explain 'Why Flutter?' to a startup founder, best first.

task.prompt: Rank these ways to explain 'Why Flutter?' to a startup founder, best first.

items.label: It is what our developers like most
Because it is trendy right now
One codebase for iOS and Android, so phase 1 ships faster and costs less to maintain
Flutter uses the Dart language and a widget tree compiled ahead of time

task.explanation: Founders care about speed, cost and maintenance. Technical detail is secondary, and personal or trend reasons do not answer their concern.

prompt: A client with an existing Laravel (PHP) web app asks you to build a new customer portal. Your team works in both Laravel and Node.js.

task.prompt: A client with an existing Laravel (PHP) web app asks you to build a new customer portal. Your team works in both Laravel and Node.js.

steps.question: What should guide the backend choice?
options: Random choice
Fit with their existing system and team, so the portal is easy to integrate and maintain
Whatever is newest
Whatever is cheapest to host this month
steps.explanation: Reusing the existing stack reduces integration work and keeps maintenance simple for their team.

steps.question: The client asks: 'Is PHP outdated?' How do you answer?
options: Agree it is outdated and push a rewrite
Say you do not know
Change the subject
Explain that Laravel is widely used and actively maintained, and that matching their current system lowers cost and risk
steps.explanation: A calm, factual answer tied to their interests builds trust; pushing a rewrite they do not need does not.

prompt: A client needs a marketing site that must rank well on Google, plus a logged-in dashboard. Rank these frontend approaches for the marketing pages, best first.

task.prompt: A client needs a marketing site that must rank well on Google, plus a logged-in dashboard. Rank these frontend approaches for the marketing pages, best first.

items.label: A pure client-side single-page app with no server rendering
Server-rendered or statically generated pages (e.g. Next.js)
A content management system site with good SEO plugins

task.explanation: Server-rendered or static pages are fast and easily indexed; a CMS also works well for marketing; a client-only SPA is weaker for SEO; a mobile app does not rank on Google at all.

prompt: A client's CTO joins the call and asks why you propose React Native instead of two native apps.

task.prompt: A client's CTO joins the call and asks why you propose React Native instead of two native apps.

steps.question: What is the strongest answer?
options: Because it is easier for our sales team to explain
Shared code means faster delivery and one team, and native modules can still be added for device-specific features
React Native is always faster than native in every case
Native apps are obsolete
steps.explanation: An honest trade-off answer works with a CTO: shared code and speed, with native escape hatches.

steps.question: The CTO asks when you would recommend fully native instead. What do you say?
options: Never
Only when the client pays more
When the app has a login screen
When the app depends heavily on advanced device features or top graphics performance, such as AR or complex games
steps.explanation: Showing when the other option wins shows judgement, not just a sales preference.

prompt: Mark the problems in this 'Technology' section of a proposal for a small business owner.

task.prompt: Mark the problems in this 'Technology' section of a proposal for a small business owner.

segments.text: Mobile app: Flutter, one codebase for iOS and Android.
Backend: Microservices on Kubernetes with event sourcing, CQRS and a service mesh.
segments.issue: Heavy architecture for a small business adds cost and complexity it does not need, and the jargon is unexplained.

segments.text: Hosting: managed cloud hosting, with backups.
You will own the code and all hosting accounts.
Stack may change at any time without notice to you.
segments.issue: Major stack changes should be agreed with the client; this undermines trust.

prompt: A client asks what a 'backend' is. Which explanation is best?

options: The part users do not see: the server, database and logic that store data and run the app's rules
The app's colour scheme
The App Store listing
The login screen
mcq.explanation: The backend handles data, business rules and integrations behind the screens users see.

prompt: When explaining a tech stack to a non-technical founder, what should you focus on?

options: What each choice means for cost, speed, scaling and maintenance
The full list of libraries and versions
Which language your developers prefer
Benchmarks from programming forums
mcq.explanation: Founders decide on business impact; translate tech choices into those terms.

prompt: A client insists on a stack your team rarely uses because a friend recommended it. What is the best response?

options: Agree and quietly learn it on their budget
Refuse the project
Say the friend is wrong without explaining
Explain the trade-offs honestly, including your team's experience, and recommend the option that serves their goals
mcq.explanation: Honest trade-offs let the client make an informed choice; hiding a skills gap leads to delays and lost trust.
